title.en: 'If only people knew what a tick could do' - the deadly meat allergies caused by tick bites
title.zh: “如果人们知道蜱虫能做什么就好了”——蜱虫叮咬引起致命的肉类过敏

summary.en: Mammalian meat allergy is a growing problem along Australia's east coast - and it's caused by tick bites.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
When Myfanwy Webb looks back at her birthday party five years ago, she is overcome with regret - remembering what she now sees as a missed opportunity to save her son's life.

Hours after a celebratory lunch at a restaurant Jeremy began having difficulty breathing. His parents called an ambulance, and the then-15-year-old began vomiting.

At the hospital, doctors noted that Jeremy had a suspected meat allergy, but ultimately blamed the episode on his asthma, which he'd had since he was a toddler. He was sent home the next day.

"I made the wrong decision," Webb says, wishing she had asked for more testing. If she had, doctors might have established that Jeremy had actually been suffering from anaphylaxis, and sent him home with an EpiPen.

​​Just over a year later, in June 2022, Jeremy died after eating a beef sausage on a camping trip with friends at a beach north of Sydney.

The cause of death was initially recorded simply as asthma. But in February, after an inquest pushed for by his family, a coroner ruled that the asthma attack and resulting fatal anaphylaxis was triggered by tick-induced mammalian meat allergy (MMA).

His death is the first in the world known to have been caused by MMA, also known as alpha-gal syndrome.

Diagnosed cases of MMA have steadily escalated since 2007, when an Australian doctor first discovered the allergy was linked to tick bites. Now, scientists and campaigners are warning that the condition, though easily prevented, can be unexpectedly triggered - and could pose a deadly threat.

Webb had long suspected that her son had a meat allergy, but it was never formally diagnosed and the family had no idea it could be fatal.

"When I looked up the research about it, there wasn't at that time anything to suggest it was more than a food intolerance."

Symptoms of the allergy can range from mild to severe including skin rashes, swelling, stomach cramps, vomiting and anaphylaxis, which can be life-threatening.

From around the age of 10 Jeremy had suffered nausea after eating meat, or even occasionally after inhaling the fumes from roast meat – which Webb believes may have set off the episode after her birthday party. On another occasion he had been hospitalised after eating marshmallows, which usually contain gelatin derived from animal parts.

It was Prof Sheryl van Nunen who discovered the link between MMA and ticks almost 20 years ago, after noticing a correlation in patients at her Sydney allergy clinic.

Working on Australia's east coast, she inadvertently found herself in one of the world's two MMA hotspots. The other is in the US - although cases of the allergy have since been noted on all six continents where ticks live.

title.en: AliExpress hit with record EU fine
title.zh: 速卖通（AliExpress）被欧盟处以创纪录罚款

summary.en: The Chinese retailer AliExpress has received a substantial fine from the European Union, becoming the latest online marketplace to be penalized under the EU’s Digital Services Act.
summary.zh: 中国零售商速卖通（AliExpress）被欧盟处以巨额罚款，成为最新一家因违反欧盟《数字服务法案》而受到处罚的在线市场。

body.en:
The Chinese retailer has become the latest major online marketplace to face penalties under the EU’s Digital Services Act.

AliExpress said it plans to appeal a penalty imposed by European Union (EU) regulators, who found shortcomings in the firm's efforts to curb illegal, unsafe and counterfeit goods.

The largest Chinese e-commerce platform in the EU, AliExpress, has been fined  €550 million ($629 million) for failing to tackle sales of illegal, unsafe and counterfeit products.

"The spread of counterfeit clothing, unsafe toys, dangerous cosmetics and other illegal and harmful products is not an unavoidable cost of shopping online - it is a failure by AliExpress to comply with its obligations under the Digital Services Act," European Commission Vice President Henna Virkkunen said on Monday.

It is the largest fine ever imposed under the Digital Services Act (DSA) , which sets out clear rules for online services in the EU, targeting especially very large online platforms.

AliExpress said it will appeal the "disproportionate" fine, saying it considers the penalty excessive.

The online retail giant, which belongs to the Alibaba Group, must pay the fine and has until October 20, to submit a plan to address the breaches. EU regulators will then review the plan, after which the company could face further penalties.

A year ago, AliExpress agreed to tighten controls on illegal and potentially dangerous goods, such as medicines and supplements. But the European Commission said the measures did not fully resolve its broader concerns.

But AliExpress said the EU's decision "ignores our sound risk management framework and the significant, proactive enhancements we have made."

The company also said it has worked with the Commission to meet its "evolving expectations."

According to the EU, AliExpress has 193 million users in the bloc, ahead of online fashion giant Shein and retailer Temu, which have 156 million and 130 million users, respectively.

"One in five Europeans say they shop once a month from Shein, Temu and AliExpress," Virkkunen said.

Temu was fined  €200 million in May , while Elon Musk's social media platform X was fined in December last year, both for DSA violations.

title.en: Yemen's Houthis announce 'maritime embargo' on Saudi Arabia
title.zh: 也门胡塞武装宣布对沙特阿拉伯实施“海上禁运”

summary.en: The Houthis say the embargo begins immediately and is a response to a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Yemen.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Iran-backed group's military spokesman said it would begin immediately and was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen.

He gave few details about the embargo but a Houthi media official said they were closing the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the southern gateway to the Red Sea, to Saudi vessels.

The Red Sea has become crucial for oil shipments from Saudi Arabia during the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

It comes a week after the most significant escalation in the largely dormant conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia since an informal truce took effect in 2022.

The Houthis said they had launched missiles at Abha airport in south-western Saudi Arabia in response to air strikes on Sanaa's airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The strikes were claimed by the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, which said it had wanted to prevent an Iranian plane from landing in the capital without authorisation.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

The fighting has reportedly left more than 150,000 people dead and triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with more than 22 million people in need of some form of aid, according to the UN.

On Monday, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said Saudi Arabia had imposed an "unjust and oppressive siege on our dear people for nearly 12 years, plundering our resources and imposing a comprehensive blockade on our ports and airports by land, sea, and air".

He then announced that the group had decided to respond by declaring a "maritime embargo against the criminal Saudi enemy, based on the equation of 'an eye for an eye'".

"Any foolish act committed by the reckless Saudi enemy through all escalation will be met with a comprehensive and decisive escalation," he added.

Sarea did not provide any further information about the embargo, but the deputy head of the Houthi media office, Nasruddin Amer, wrote on X that the group's forces were "closing Bab al-Mandab to Saudi enemy ships".

The Bab al-Mandab Strait, a 32km-wide (20-mile) waterway located between south-western Yemen and the Horn of Africa. It connects the Gulf of Aden with the Red Sea, which is linked to the Mediterranean by the Suez canal.

Soon after the start of the Gaza war in October 2023, the Houthis began attacking merchant vessels in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden with missiles, drones and small boats, saying they were acting in support of the Palestinians.

title.en: Notorious drug cartel leader Ismael Zambada sentenced to life in US prison
title.zh: 臭名昭著的贩毒集团头目伊斯梅尔·赞巴达在美国被判处终身监禁

summary.en: Ismael Zambada, known as "El Mayo" and co-founder of the Sinaloa Cartel, has been sentenced to life in a US prison. He was also ordered to pay $15 billion after admitting to trafficking large quantities of drugs into the United States.
summary.zh: 被称为“El Mayo”的锡那罗亚贩毒集团联合创始人伊斯梅尔·赞巴达，因承认向美国贩运大量毒品，被判处美国监狱终身监禁，并被勒令支付150亿美元。

body.en:
One of the most notorious figures in Mexico's drug cartels, Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, will spend the rest of his life in prison, a US judge ruled has ruled, two years after Zambada was lured to the US in an elaborate sting operation.

The 76-year-old, who founded the violent Sinaloa Cartel with Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzmán, was also ordered to pay $15bn (£11bn).

In 2024, El Chapo's son led Zambada to believe they were travelling to northern Mexico to inspect clandestine airstrips, when their plane instead landed in Texas and he was arrested.

Last year, Zambada reached a plea deal and admitted to drug smuggling and conspiracy charges in exchange for avoiding the death penalty.

On Monday, US District Judge Brian Cogan sentenced Zambada during a hearing in Brooklyn federal court. His guilty plea carried a mandatory term of life in prison, Reuters reported.

The $15bn he was ordered to pay represents drug-trafficking profits from his role as the principal leader of a criminal enterprise, according to the justice department.

El Chapo's son, Joaquin Guzmán Lopez, was also arrested in July 2024 and has pleaded guilty to federal drug charges. He has yet to be sentenced.

In the plea deal , Zambada officially accepted his role in creating the vast criminal network which has sent huge amounts of cocaine and other drugs into the US since he co-founded the Sinaloa Cartel at the end of the 1980s.

"Ismael Zambada Garcia spent nearly four decades poisoning American communities to make billions of dollars in profit and ordering the murders of anyone who stood in his way," said US Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr for the Eastern District of New York in a statement.

Prosecutors argued in a sentencing memo that Zambada "was one of the most-if not the most-prolific and powerful narcotraffickers in the world", according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

The Sinaloa Cartel has been at war with itself since Zambada was taken into custody and has wreaked mayhem across the Mexican state of Sinaloa. Hundreds of people have been reported missing during fighting between its two rival factions.

Violence and bloodletting also shook the cartel after El Chapo was arrested and extradited to the US in 2016, as factions wrestled for control of territory while fighting off opposing drug gangs who sensed weakness. He is also serving life in prison.

One of the issues that has arisen since Zambada agreed to plead guilty has been where he will serve his sentence.

He has requested to be sent to a prison hospital, saying he will need medical care for age-related health issues.

Federal prosecutors, though, are seeking a higher-level of incarceration, contending Zambada still poses a security threat while beyond bars and could continue to direct illegal drug operations.

title.en: Trump says US strikes hit Iran in 'honour' of American soldiers killed
title.zh: 特朗普称美军袭击伊朗是为了“纪念”遇难美军士兵

summary.en: US strikes in the Middle East, described by President Trump as being in 'honour' of American soldiers killed, were followed by Iranian attacks in Syria and Jordan. Reports also indicate two ships exploded in the Strait of Hormuz amidst the escalating tensions.
summary.zh: 美国总统特朗普表示，美军在中东的袭击是为了“纪念”遇害的美国士兵，随后伊朗在叙利亚和约旦发动了袭击。另据报道，在局势不断升级之际，霍尔木兹海峡有两艘船只发生爆炸。

body.en:
President Donald Trump has said the latest strikes by the US hit Iran "very hard", adding that the attacks were "in honour" of three US soldiers killed in recent days - two in Jordan, one in Iraq.

US Central Command (Centcom) said its strikes - conducted for the ninth consecutive night - had targeted military sites and communications networks to "further diminish" Iran's attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Blasts were heard across Iran.

Iran said it had responded with a "surprise attack" in Syria and targeted US aircraft at Jordan's Aqaba airport.

Later on Monday, Trump warned that "every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over".

Elsewhere in the region, Kuwait's armed forces said they had intercepted Iranian drones.

On the US strikes, Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency reported that several cities had been hit including Tabriz, Chabahar, Konarak, Bandar Mahshahr and Bandar Imam Khomeini.

There were also Iranian state media reports that two oil tankers had exploded as the vessels tried to cross the strait.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said the tankers were going through what it called an "unsafe and hazardous southern route" of the strait and "exploded and were brought to a halt". Centcom disputed the claims.

The IRGC added that the strait "will not be safe for the transit of petrochemical products, nor even a single drop of oil and gas" as long as the US strikes continue and that it will respond with a "punitive operation".

Over the weekend, the US confirmed that a service member had been killed after an Iranian attack in northern Iraq on Saturday.

That news came after the US said a separate attack on a base in Jordan on Friday had killed two soldiers there. The two have now been identified by the Pentagon as Pte Isabella Gonzales, 19, and Lt Tyler James Feehan, 25.

A third service member was declared missing after the attack in Jordan, and US officials say "unidentified remains" have been found during the search process.

As the strikes continued over the weekend, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the US "always remains open to a diplomatic solution".

He also said "the world has to decide whether or not it's going to allow an international waterway to be under the control" of Iran, saying Tehran was using the crucial shipping route as leverage.

His comments come as a preliminary deal made in mid-June to stop fighting has unravelled, with negotiations for a permanent peace making little progress after Trump declared the agreement was "over" on 8 July.
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，美国最近的袭击对伊朗造成了“非常沉重的打击”，并补充说，这些袭击是为了“纪念”最近几天阵亡的三名美国士兵，其中两人在约旦，一人在伊拉克。 当地时间周一凌晨，美国中央司令部（Centcom）表示，伊朗各地传出爆炸声，已连续第九晚发动“新一波”打击。 美国表示，它已将军事地点和通信网络作为目标，以“进一步减少”德黑兰对霍尔木兹海峡船只的袭击。 伊朗表示，它在叙利亚发动了“突然袭击”，并针对约旦亚喀巴机场的美国飞机进行了回应。 在该地区其他地方，科威特武装部队表示他们拦截了伊朗无人机。 关于美国的空袭，伊朗半官方通讯社塔斯尼姆通讯社报道称，包括大不里士、恰巴哈尔、科纳拉克、马赫沙赫尔港和伊玛目霍梅尼港在内的多个城市遭到袭击。 伊朗官方媒体也报道称，两艘油轮在试图穿越海峡时发生爆炸。 伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）表示，这些油轮当时正在通过所谓的海峡“不安全且危险的南部路线”，并“爆炸并被迫停下来”。中央司令部对这些说法提出异议。 伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队补充说，只要美国继续发动袭击，该海峡“对于石化产品的过境来说就不安全，甚至一滴石油和天然气也不安全”，并表示将采取“惩罚性行动”予以回应。 周末，美国证实，周六伊朗在伊拉克​​北部发动袭击后，一名军人死亡。 这一消息是在美国表示周五对约旦一个基地的另一次袭击造成两名士兵死亡之后发布的。五角大楼现已确认这两人分别为 19 岁的伊莎贝拉·冈萨雷斯上尉和 25 岁的泰勒·詹姆斯·费汉中尉。 约旦袭击事件发生后，第三名军人被宣布失踪，美国官员表示，在搜索过程中发现了“身份不明的遗骸”。 随着周末美国和伊朗之间的袭击仍在继续，美国国务卿马可·卢比奥表示，美国“始终对外交解决方案持开放态度”。 他还表示，“世界必须决定是否允许国际水道处于伊朗的控制之下”，并表示德黑兰正在利用这条重要的航线作为杠杆。 他发表此番言论之际，6月中旬达成的一项停止战斗的初步协议已经瓦解，特朗普于7月8日宣布该协议“结束”后，永久和平谈判几乎没有取得任何进展。

reflection.en: The escalating cycle of strikes and counter-strikes highlights the tragic reality that violence often begets more violence. Yahweh's words remind us that those who live by the sword often face its consequences, urging a deeper reflection on how to break such destructive patterns.
reflection.zh: 这种不断升级的打击与反击循环，凸显了暴力往往会滋生更多暴力的悲剧性现实。雅伟的话语提醒我们，那些动刀的，必死在刀下，这促使我们更深地反思如何打破这种破坏性的模式。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: ‘All I think about is her’: Families demand answers as Nigeria's boat disasters keep happening
title.zh: “我只想着她”：尼日利亚船只灾难频发，家属要求给出解释

summary.en: Hundreds of lives are lost annually in Nigeria due to recurring boat accidents, yet the situation remains unchanged. Grieving families are now demanding accountability and action from authorities.
summary.zh: 尼日利亚每年有数百人死于船只事故，但情况似乎没有改变。悲痛的家庭正在要求当局给出解释并采取行动。

body.en:
Many die in a boat accident; officials say the regulations should be followed; their calls are ignored; campaigners say the resources are not available; another tragedy happens.

This time, a search-and-rescue team is looking for survivors of a capsized wooden canoe in Jigawa state.

Forty were thought to be on board, mostly female farmers and labourers, when it sank on Sunday. Twenty-three people have been rescued alive but nine bodies have been recovered from the river so far.

Last month, a boat accident on the River Benue in central Nigeria claimed the lives of 12 people, including a pregnant woman and six children.

Earlier this year , 14 people lost their lives when their boat capsized in Gumbi, Kebbi state. They had been returning from a wedding ceremony, accompanying the bride to her new husband's home.

So far this year, more than 55 people have already lost their lives in boat accidents, with dozens of bodies yet to be recovered.

For millions of Nigerians, particularly in rural areas, rivers are the most practical means of transport. With many villages on or close to waterways and few bridges and poor roads to aid travel, rickety wooden boats are often the only way for people to reach family members elsewhere, to take goods to market, or to see the outside world.

For people like Isiyaka Bello, the painful memory of losing someone to water is still fresh. Last year, his wife was returning from a village market in Kebbi state when she and eight others lost their lives.

"It seems like just yesterday. She left behind four children, and I am still struggling to adjust to raising them on my own.

After every disaster, authorities promise to do better. But on the water there is little, if any, change.

Mallam Sala Altine holds a traditional title that carries the weight of life and death on the river. He is the Sarkin Ruwan Shiroro - the man entrusted with keeping people safe on the Shiroro Lake in Niger state, where some of Nigeria's deadliest boat tragedies have occurred.

The River Niger, the third-longest in Africa, passes through the state with which it shares a name, where it is fed by numerous smaller rivers and connected waterways, creating an environment where fatal accidents are both frequent and severe.

Between January 2023 and October 2025, Niger state accounted for a significant share of the nearly 860 deaths recorded across Nigeria. One report noted 253 deaths in the state between June 2023 and August 2025.

Altine says there is a critical shortage of life jackets despite repeated government promises to supply them.

"Our boats usually carry well over 100 passengers. But most of the time, we can only provide life jackets for 10 people, or even fewer, because we simply don't have enough," he explains.

title.en: Russia says bus strike kills 5 in border region with Ukraine
title.zh: 俄罗斯称乌克兰边境地区巴士罢工造成5人死亡

summary.en: The strike comes as Ukraine launched more than hundreds of drones at Moscow after a Russian missile barrage on Kyiv, as President Zelenskyy sought to calm growing tensions over Ukraine’s military leadership.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The strike comes as Ukraine launched more than hundreds of drones at Moscow after a Russian missile barrage on Kyiv, as President Zelenskyy sought to calm growing tensions over Ukraine’s military leadership.

Russia said Monday that a Ukrainian strike on a bus in the border region of Belgorod killed five civilians, including a minor, and left three others critically injured.

The attack came after a Ukrainian retaliatory strike on Moscow, with city officials reporting that more than 400 drones targeted the Russian capital.

The latest escalation followed Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities over the weekend.

In eastern Ukraine , Russian attacks on Pavlograd and Kramatorsk killed two people in each city, according to local authorities.

Officials also reported one person killed in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia during Russian bombardment.

Ukraine targeted the Russian capital with more than 400 drones from Sunday into Monday, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.

He added that most of the drones were intercepted, but Moscow region Gov. Andrei Vorobyov said at least 10 people were wounded by Ukrainian drones.

Several residential buildings and civilian infrastructure facilities were also damaged.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces were targeting Russian logistics facilities and an oil depot in the region.

"We are responding, justly, to every Russian strike against our cities and communities," Zelenskyy said in a post on X.

Meanwhile, Ukraine's military publicly denied rumors that Zelenskyy was firing the chief of Ukraine's armed forces, Oleksandr Syrskyi.

Zelenskyy has faced criticism over the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov last week.

There have been days of protests in Ukraine following Fedorov's removal, as a long-running dispute between the reform-minded minister and Syrskyi spilled into the open.

Zelenskyy appointed Yevhenii Khmara, the acting head of Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), as acting defense minister and asked parliament to approve him for the position.

On Monday, he posted several messages on social media showing him meeting with Ukraine's top military commanders to discuss the latest developments in the war, which has dragged on for more than four years.

body.zh: 这次袭击发生之际，乌克兰在俄罗斯对基辅进行导弹袭击后向莫斯科发射了数百架无人机，泽伦斯基总统试图平息乌克兰军事领导层日益紧张的局势。 俄罗斯周一表示，乌克兰在别尔哥罗德边境地区对一辆公共汽车发动袭击，造成包括一名未成年人在内的五名平民死亡，另有三人重伤。 这次袭击发生在乌克兰对莫斯科进行报复性袭击之后，市政府官员报告称，有 400 多架无人机瞄准了俄罗斯首都。 俄罗斯周末对基辅和其他乌克兰城市发动弹道导弹袭击后，最新升级事件随之而来。 据地方当局称，在乌克兰东部，俄罗斯对巴甫洛格勒和克拉马托尔斯克的袭击造成每座城市两人死亡。 官员还报告说，南部城市扎波罗热有一人在俄罗斯轰炸中丧生。 莫斯科市长谢尔盖·索比亚宁表示，从周日到周一，乌克兰出动了 400 多架无人机瞄准俄罗斯首都。 他补充说，大部分无人机被拦截，但莫斯科地区州长安德烈·沃罗比约夫表示，至少有 10 人被乌克兰无人机炸伤。 多栋住宅楼和民用基础设施也遭到破坏。 乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示，乌克兰军队的目标是俄罗斯在该地区的后勤设施和一个油库。 泽连斯基在 X 上发帖称：“我们正在公正地回应俄罗斯针对我们城市和社区的每一次袭击。” 与此同时，乌克兰军方公开否认了泽连斯基解雇乌克兰武装部队总司令亚历山大·西尔斯基的传言。 泽伦斯基因上周解雇国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫而面临批评。 费多罗夫被免职后，乌克兰发生了数天的抗议活动，这位具有改革思想的部长与西尔斯基之间的长期争端公开化。 泽连斯基任命乌克兰安全局（SBU）代理局长叶夫海尼·赫马拉（Yevhenii Khmara）为代理国防部长，并请求议会批准他担任这一职务。 周一，他在社交媒体上发布了多条消息，显示他与乌克兰最高军事指挥官会面，讨论这场已经持续四年多的战争的最新进展。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

title.en: Guterres to visit Cyprus as UN seeks to revive peace talks
title.zh: 古特雷斯将访问塞浦路斯，联合国寻求恢复和谈

summary.en: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is scheduled to visit Cyprus next week to try and restart the stalled peace process. The visit aims to explore new avenues for dialogue and potential solutions to the long-standing conflict.
summary.zh: 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯定于下周访问塞浦路斯，旨在重启陷入僵局的和平进程。此次访问旨在探索新的对话途径和解决长期冲突的潜在方案。

body.en:
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will visit Cyprus next week in what is seen as an effort to kickstart the stalled peace process. Why now? What is known about the plan? And what might be different this time round?

Monday marks the 52nd anniversary of Turkey's 1974 invasion of Cyprus , which led to the division of the island.

Five decades later, the Cyprus issue remains one of the world's longest-running unresolved disputes.

The United Nations announced last week that Antonio Guterres  was due to visit Cyprus from July 27 to 29 — the first visit by a UN secretary-general in 16 years — in an effort to breathe new life into the stalled peace process.

His visit marks the culmination of a renewed UN initiative that was launched after an informal enlarged meeting on Cyprus held in Geneva in March.

Since then, the UN secretary-general's personal envoy, Maria Angela Holguin, has held a series of consultations in Cyprus, Greece, Turkey , the United Kingdom and Brussels to assess whether the political conditions exist for meaningful negotiations to resume.

During his stay in Cyprus, Guterres will hold separate meetings with  President of the Republic of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman.

On July 29, the two leaders are expected to meet jointly with the UN chief at the residence of the UN Special Representative in the UN-controlled buffer zone.

The last time a UN secretary-general visited Cyprus was in 2010, when Ban Ki-moon sought to inject political momentum into negotiations between then President of the Republic of Cyprus Demetris Christofias and Turkish Cypriot leader Mehmet Ali Talat.

Both leaders came from left-wing political parties that supported a bizonal, bicommunal federation and were widely seen as having the political will to pursue a comprehensive settlement.

That momentum, however, faded only months later after Talat lost the Turkish Cypriot leadership election to Dervis Eroglu, while major disagreements over the core chapters of the negotiations remained unresolved.

Ban's efforts were preceded by the intensive engagement of Kofi Annan between 2002 and 2004, when the UN undertook its most ambitious effort to broker a comprehensive settlement of the Cyprus issue.

Annan became personally involved in the negotiations, presenting a series of revised versions of what became known as the Annan Plan.

The initiative culminated in simultaneous referendums in April 2004. The proposal was approved by a majority of Turkish Cypriot voters but rejected by 75.8% of Greek Cypriot voters.

The announcement of Guterres' visit comes amid reports that the UN is exploring a possible new framework for resolving the Cyprus issue.

body.zh: 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯将于下周访问塞浦路斯，此举被视为旨在启动陷入僵局的和平进程。为什么是现在？关于该计划有哪些已知信息？这次可能会有什么不同？ 周一是土耳其 1974 年入侵塞浦路斯 52 周年，这次入侵导致了塞浦路斯岛的分裂。 五年后，塞浦路斯问题仍然是世界上持续时间最长的未解决争端之一。 联合国上周宣布，安东尼奥·古特雷斯将于 7 月 27 日至 29 日访问塞浦路斯，这是联合国秘书长 16 年来的首次访问，旨在为陷入僵局的和平进程注入新的活力。 他的访问标志着联合国新倡议的高潮，该倡议是三月份在日内瓦举行的塞浦路斯问题非正式扩大会议后发起的。 此后，联合国秘书长个人特使玛丽亚·安吉拉·奥尔金在塞浦路斯、希腊、土耳其、英国和布鲁塞尔举行了一系列磋商，以评估是否存在恢复有意义的谈判的政治条件。 在塞浦路斯逗留期间，古特雷斯将分别与塞浦路斯共和国总统尼科斯·赫里斯托杜利德斯和土族塞人领导人图凡·埃尔胡曼举行会晤。 7月29日，两国领导人预计将在位于联合国控制缓冲区的联合国特别代表官邸与联合国秘书长共同会晤。 联合国秘书长上次访问塞浦路斯是在 2010 年，当时潘基文试图为时任塞浦路斯共和国总统德米特里斯·赫里斯托菲亚斯和土族塞人领导人穆罕默德·阿里·塔拉特之间的谈判注入政治动力。 两位领导人都来自支持两区两族联邦的左翼政党，并被广泛认为具有寻求全面解决方案的政治意愿。 然而，几个月后，塔拉特在土族塞人领导人选举中输给德尔维斯·埃罗格鲁后，这种势头就消退了，而谈判核心章节的重大分歧仍未解决。 在潘基文做出努力之前，科菲·安南在 2002 年至 2004 年期间大力参与，当时联合国为促成塞浦路斯问题的全面解决做出了最雄心勃勃的努力。 安南亲自参与了谈判，提出了一系列被称为“安南计划”的修订版本。 该倡议最终于 2004 年 4 月同时举行全民公投。该提案获得大多数土族塞人选民的批准，但遭到 75.8% 希族塞人选民的拒绝。 古特雷斯宣布访问之际，有报道称联合国正在探索解决塞浦路斯问题的可能新框架。 英国《独立报》发表后，讨论愈演愈烈……

title.en: Why a 90-year-old treaty limits NATO in the Black Sea
title.zh: 一项90年前的条约为何限制北约进入黑海

summary.en: A 90-year-old international treaty continues to restrict NATO's naval access to the Black Sea, influencing the balance of power as Ukraine continues its conflict with Russia. This historical agreement poses challenges for NATO's ability to project military strength into the region.
summary.zh: 一项有90年历史的国际条约持续限制北约海军进入黑海，在乌克兰与俄罗斯的冲突中影响着力量平衡。这项历史性协议对北约在该地区投射军事力量的能力构成了挑战。

body.en:
A 90-year-old treaty still shapes the balance of power in the Black Sea. As Ukraine fights on against Russia, can NATO project power into waters it can't enter freely?

Now more than four years after  Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine , the Black Sea has become one of Europe's key security frontiers. And yet, it is currently "quite empty of warships," Thomas de Waal, a senior fellow at Carnegie Europe, told DW. This, he said, "is a bit of a paradox." To understand that paradox, we first need to need to take a closer look at the map.

The Black Sea is bordered by six countries: Turkey , Bulgaria , Romania , Ukraine , Russia , and Georgia . The first three on that list are part of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, or NATO — the other three are not. To make matters more complicated, two of the latter three are at war with each other.

Access to the Black Sea runs through a single, narrow bottleneck. To get there, a ship coming from the Mediterranean Sea  would have to pass the Dardanelles Straits and the Bosporus, which crosses through the heart of Turkey's largest metropolis Istanbul .

At its narrowest point, the Bosporus is just 700 meters (0.4 miles) wide. For comparison, another critical passageway currently in the headlines is the Strait of Hormuz , which is approximately 33 kilometers (21 miles) wide at its narrowest point.

It is this geographic bottleneck to the Black Sea that makes it "an economic choke point," said de Waal. "Whoever controls the Turkish Straits also controls, to some extent, trade through the Black Sea and also has an enormous military advantage."

Russia also has a special interest in the Black Sea, according to Daria Isachenko, a visiting fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs. "A strong military position in the Black Sea for Russia is not an end in itself, but also a means to advance its geopolitical ambitions beyond and also strengthen its great power status."

The second part of the equation goes back to a treaty signed exactly 90 years ago.

On July 20, 1936, representatives from just under a dozen countries gathered in the Swiss town of Montreux to settle a long-standing dilemma: How — and by whom — should these vital waterways be governed? They established the Montreux Convention, an agreement that essentially restored Turkey's sovereignty over the Dardanelles Strait and Bosporus. This came after years of international oversight, following the Ottoman Empire's defeat in the First World War . 

Negotiations resulted in a document of nearly 30 pages, which set the legal framework that governs the Turkish Straits to this day. The treaty keeps the straits open to passenger and commercial traffic during peacetime — crucial for the important...
body.zh: 一项已有 90 年历史的条约仍然决定着黑海的力量平衡。在乌克兰与俄罗斯交战之际，北约能否将兵力投射到它无法自由进入的水域？ 俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰四年多后，黑海已成为欧洲重要的安全前沿之一。然而，卡内基欧洲研究中心高级研究员托马斯·德瓦尔(Thomas de Waal)告诉德国之声，目前“几乎没有军舰”。他说，这“有点悖论”。要理解这个悖论，我们首先需要仔细观察地图。 黑海与六个国家接壤：土耳其、保加利亚、罗马尼亚、乌克兰、俄罗斯和格鲁吉亚。该名单上的前三个是北大西洋公约组织（NATO）的一部分，而其他三个则不是。使事情变得更加复杂的是，后三个中的两个相互交战。 进入黑海需要经过一个狭窄的瓶颈。要到达那里，来自地中海的船只必须经过达达尼尔海峡和博斯普鲁斯海峡，博斯普鲁斯海峡穿过土耳其最大的大都市伊斯坦布尔的中心。 博斯普鲁斯海峡最窄处仅 700 米（0.4 英里）宽。相比之下，目前成为头条新闻的另一个重要通道是霍尔木兹海峡，其最窄处宽约 33 公里（21 英里）。 德瓦尔说，正是黑海的地理瓶颈使其成为“经济瓶颈”。 “谁控制了土耳其海峡，就在某种程度上控制了黑海贸易，并且拥有巨大的军事优势。” 德国国际与安全事务研究所客座研究员达里亚·伊萨琴科表示，俄罗斯对黑海也有着特殊的兴趣。 “对俄罗斯来说，在黑海拥有强大的军事地位本身并不是目的，而是超越其地缘政治野心并加强其大国地位的一种手段。” 等式的第二部分可以追溯到 90 年前签署的一项条约。 1936 年 7 月 20 日，来自十几个国家的代表齐聚瑞士小镇蒙特勒，解决一个长期存在的难题：这些重要水道应该如何以及由谁来管理？他们建立了《蒙特勒公约》，该协议基本上恢复了土耳其对达达尼尔海峡和博斯普鲁斯海峡的主权。这是奥斯曼帝国在第一次世界大战中战败后经过多年的国际监督。 谈判达成了一份近 30 页的文件，制定了迄今为止管辖土耳其海峡的法律框架。该条约在和平时期保持海峡对客运和商业交通开放——这对于重要的……

title.en: Israel's embassy takes rare swipe at Labor's platform on eve of conference

summary.en: The four-page statement drew a shrug from a member of Labor's front bench.

body.en:
Israel's embassy has rebuked the Labor party's draft national platform, warning its wording on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict places sole "responsibility" on the Jewish state while overlooking the role of Hamas and Palestinian leadership.

The four-page statement is a highly unusual intervention by a foreign government ahead of the party's national conference in Adelaide.

Labor's 2026 platform, which outlines the party's priorities and beliefs, contains an expanded statement on "Israel and Palestine" following the government's move to recognise Palestinian statehood, a longstanding part of the party platform.

The document reiterates support for a two-state solution, and also says the party "unreservedly condemns terrorism and violent extremism, including as perpetrated by Hamas and other extremists," stating Israelis and Palestinians deserve to live their lives free from terror and violence.

The platform says Israel "must comply with obligations as an occupying power" in supplying food and medical supplies for Palestinian civilians under international humanitarian law, and also condemns recent Knesset laws around the death penalty as "discriminatory."

The 'Death Penalty for Terrorists' law passed in March — and a subsequent 2026 military tribunal law — mandate capital punishment for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks. The United Nations Human Rights Office warned the laws breach international humanitarian law and could amount to war crimes.

The unsigned Israeli embassy statement, released on Monday, reads: "The Embassy respectfully submits that several elements of the draft National Platform risk placing responsibility for the conflict on one party while giving insufficient attention to the decisions, conduct and continuing obligations of the Palestinian leadership and terrorist organisations such as Hamas."

"Israel has repeatedly demonstrated its willingness to make difficult compromises when genuine peace is possible."

While continuing to oppose Palestinian recognition, which the Australian government declared sovereign and independent in September 2025, Israel's embassy also disputed language in the draft platform condemning "extremist settler violence," which the government in June warned was at "horrific levels".

The embassy said settler violence "receives disproportionate attention," labelling it a "reprehensible but marginal phenomenon".

UN monitors have documented over 1,000 Israeli settler attacks causing casualties or property damage this year, averaging six incidents per day and resulting in the displacement of more than 2,200 Palestinians.

body.en:
On Sunday, social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested in Miami in the United States, after authorities in the United Kingdom issued 38 new charges against the brothers, deepening the pair's international legal saga and adding further complication to an already fraught legal situation.

The United Kingdom's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has charged the brothers — who deny all wrongdoing — with fresh counts of rape, actual bodily harm, and human trafficking.

The new accusations add to a mountain of serious charges against the pair and could lead to the brothers' extradition from the US, assuming it is approved by the US state department.

Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate are dual US-UK citizens who have risen to prominence as social media influencers.

Andrew started his career in public life as a kickboxer and has gone on to become a prominent figure in the online 'manosphere' space, describing himself as a misogynist and encouraging his more than 10 million followers to follow in his footsteps.

He primarily posts on X, having been banned from YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram for violating hate speech guidelines.

Stephanie Wescott, a lecturer in humanities and social science at Monash University, described Andrew as the "main character" of this content, while his brother Tristan is more of a "side figure".

She said the Tates have turned disrespecting and abusing women into a business model that glamorises male dominance, 'teaching' men how to emulate them through an online academy.

"[They promote] anti-feminism, anti-gender-equality, and hyper-masculinity or, you know, 'men being men' or men going back to a type of manhood that no longer exists," she said.

"One of their business models has been to train other young men into becoming the sort of influencers that they claim that they are.

"Part of that business model has also been to exploit and harm the girls and women around you and to use their images as currency to sell online — we know Australian men have signed up for these services.

The pair have also expressed support for US President Donald Trump, and Trump's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr, spoke out against the brothers' detention in Romania in 2023.

"The other layer to this is, of course, that they have this incredible political proximity to Donald Trump," Wescott said.

In 2025, Andrew Tate said he was "very close with the Trump family". Trump himself has said little about the Tates, however.

"They have been supported and aided by adjacent figures, podcasters such as Joe Rogan and others like him," Wescott continued.

title.en: Nigel Farage's unusual UK by-election now has an Australian candidate
title.zh: 奈杰尔·法拉奇不寻常的英国补选现有一名澳大利亚候选人

summary.en: Nigel Farage will compete in the Clacton by-election against several candidates, including Count Binface and Australian Daniel Pocock.
summary.zh: 奈杰尔·法拉奇将在克拉克顿补选中与包括宾费斯伯爵和澳大利亚人丹尼尔·波科克在内的多位候选人竞争。

body.en:
There's a man with a bin on his head, three people representing the Monster Raving Loony Party, Nigel Farage and an Australian — now all vying for the seat vacated by the Reform UK leader in a crucial by-election.

The Clacton by-election, triggered by the parliamentary resignation of Farage over a donations scandal, has attracted all sorts of profiles to the mix.

Farage, who is under investigation over millions of pounds' worth of undeclared gifts and donations from wealthy backers, quit parliament earlier this month to trigger a by-election, but said he would re-contest his seat . The Reform UK leader said he wanted voters in his electoral district in south-east England to judge his actions, not what he said was a liberal "establishment" bent on discrediting him.

Farage is widely expected to win the seat again, and is the only mainstream candidate running, after other major parties said they would refuse to take part in what they characterised as a stunt.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

A number of joke candidates — including Count Binface and another called 'Nick the Incredible Flying Brick' — are vying for the seat, along with 20 independents.

Pocock is a Swiss-Irish-Australian software engineer who describes himself as an "expert on cybersecurity, open source software [and] cryptocurrencies".

According to his website, he was born in the Melbourne suburb of Coburg before moving to rural Wandong. He graduated from the University of Melbourne in 2002 with a Bachelor of Computer Science.

While studying, he joined the National Union of Students and used his technical skills to assist websites for early social causes. He built a website opposing the death penalty after Schapelle Corby's arrest in Bali on drug trafficking charges.

He moved to Europe after graduation and worked for companies like Barclays Capital, Thomson Reuters, and UBS.

In a press release announcing his candidacy, Pocock says he was spurred to nominate himself for Clacton by the prospect of "novelty candidates".

"If the Essex Lion was to appear on the ballot paper, I suspect it would have an equally good chance of winning. I have yet to see a single report about the real, day-to-day issues facing residents of the district," he said.

"In a parody of this situation, I have chosen the codename Pocock-on-Sea for the operation to unleash an Australian upon London's Establishment."

title.en: 'Impossible': Nauru community detainees say Australian funds not enough to buy food with
title.zh: “不可能”：瑙鲁社区被拘留者称澳大利亚资金不足以购买食物

summary.en: They face a choice between paying for food, water or internet.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Asylum seekers being detained within the community in Nauru are struggling to buy enough food and are being forced to choose between eating and paying for other necessities.

The difficulties are being driven by a mix of high living costs and low income support, according to a new report by the Asylum Seeker Resource Centre.

Of 78 people interviewed for the report, 99 per cent said they couldn't afford to buy enough food with their current allowance.

On top of that, 68 per cent said they rarely or never had access to fresh fruit, vegetables and meat, and 82 per cent said they didn't have easy access to free, clean drinking water.

Community detainees live on $260 a fortnight to cover all of their basic needs outside accommodation.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The group have been sent to the tiny island nation under Australia's long-standing policy of offshore processing for asylum-seekers who arrive by boat.

Speaking anonymously, detainees consistently told the centre the allowance wasn't enough to sustain them, forcing them to decide between buying food and other necessities like clothing and internet access.

Many were running out of money before their next payment and were forced to reduce meals or go without food altogether.

"With food we have to compromise, if you buy vegetables you can't afford rice. If you buy meat, you can't afford fruit," one said.

"The money is not enough because everything is expensive here — rice, fish, we cannot buy any fruit here, internet for $100 per month, how is it possible to survive?" said another.

Nauru struggles with food insecurity due to its remote location and limited local agriculture, with perishable food flown in weekly and often selling out quickly or being prohibitively expensive.

With no rivers or freshwater lakes, the island also relies primarily on rainwater harvesting and desalination, meaning water shortages are common during times of low rainfall, forcing those who live there to turn to bottled water.

Asylum seekers in the community often struggle due to their lack of orientation or local knowledge as to how food systems work, as well as infrequent transportation to and from markets, the resource centre said.

As of 31 May, there were 101 people seeking asylum in Nauru, 91 of whom were in community accommodation.

The majority of those in detention in Nauru were young to middle-aged men from south and east Asia.

The group of asylum seekers are separate from a group of hundreds of former immigration detainees, known as the NZYQ cohort, sent to Nauru from Australia after the High Court in 2024 ruled indefinite detention to be unlawful.

title.en: Food delivery rider wins China's top literary prize
title.zh: 外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖

summary.en: Wang Jibing, a food delivery rider, has been awarded China's most prestigious literary prize. His achievement highlights a growing trend of blue-collar workers in China gaining recognition for their literary contributions.
summary.zh: 外卖骑手王计兵荣获中国最高文学奖。他的成就凸显了中国蓝领工人因其文学作品而获得更广泛关注的趋势。

body.en:
A collection of poems, some scribbled on slips of paper between food deliveries, has won Wang Jibing one of China's top literary honours.

Low Flight, inspired by the everyday challenges delivery riders face, has bagged the Lu Xun Literary Prize - named after a writer who has been referred to as the father of modern Chinese literature.

Wang, 56, who became a delivery rider around 2019, gained traction on social media for his poems and essays.

He is part of a growing group of blue-collar workers who are being celebrated for their literary works, which offer a glimpse into the pressures that they face in China's massive gig economy.

For Wang, the prestigious literary prize comes after a few difficult decades as an odd job worker.

"I held my breath and felt extremely nervous… Once it was revealed, everything was settled," Wang told state media outlet Global Times on 15 July, when news broke that he had won the award - adding that the media attention around him had created a lot of mental pressure on him.

The monetary awards for recipients of the Lu Xun Literary Prize are not publicly announced - though as of 2014 it stood at 100,000 Chinese yuan ($14,800; £11,000).

Born in Jiangsu province, Wang left school as a teenager due to financial hardship at home. He took on various jobs, from construction to scavenging for waste and selling things at a street stall, before becoming a food deliveryman.

But his love for reading persisted, and over the last decade he has been posting his own poems and essays on social media.

In 2022, one of his poems, titled Man in a Hurry, went viral online. It was inspired by a incident in 2019, in which he spent hours on a frustrating delivery after a customer entered the wrong address.

In 2023 he published his first poetry collection, Man in a Hurry: Poems of a Food Delivery Rider.

Despite winning the award, Wang told the outlet he had no intention of quitting his job, adding that he planned to work until he turns 60.

"Financially I don't need this job to make a living, but I love the vibe of the work and it keeps me fit," said the Global Times report. "I want a down-to-earth life and the award will never change who I am."

Low Flight, published in 2024, is a collection of poems inspired by interviews and surveys that Wang conducted with around 200 delivery riders.

"Who says spreading your wings means flying high? Flying low is also flying," goes one of the lines in his poems.

His win comes as a growing number of blue worker collars in China have in recent years been making their mark in the literary world.

body.zh: 王吉兵的一本诗集（其中一些是在送餐期间写在纸条上的）为他赢得了中国最高文学荣誉之一。 《低空飞行》的灵感来自于外卖骑手每天面临的挑战，它获得了鲁迅文学奖——以一位被称为中国现代文学之父的作家的名字命名。 王现年 56 岁，2019 年左右成为一名送货骑手，他的诗歌和散文在社交媒体上受到关注。 他是越来越多的蓝领工人群体中的一员，这些工人因其文学作品而受到赞誉，这让人们得以一窥他们在中国庞大的零工经济中面临的压力。 对于王来说，享有盛誉的文学奖是在他作为打零工经历了几十年艰难的生活之后获得的。 7月15日，当他获奖的消息传出时，王告诉官方媒体《环球时报》：“我屏住呼吸，感到非常紧张……一旦揭晓，一切就都解决了。”他还补充说，周围媒体的关注给他带来了很大的精神压力。 鲁迅文学奖获奖者的奖金并未公开公布，但截至 2014 年，奖金为 10 万元人民币（14,800 美元；11,000 英镑）。 王出生于江苏省，青少年时期因家庭经济困难而辍学。在成为一名送餐员之前，他从事过各种工作，从建筑到清理垃圾，再到在街边摊上卖东西。 但他对阅读的热爱始终如一，在过去的十年里，他一直在社交媒体上发布自己的诗歌和散文。 2022年，他的一首诗《匆忙的男人》在网上疯传。它的灵感来自 2019 年的一次事件，当时一位顾客输入了错误的地址，他花了几个小时处理令人沮丧的送货事宜。 2023年，他出版了第一部诗集《匆忙的人：送餐骑手的诗》。 尽管获奖，王告诉媒体他无意辞职，并补充说他计划工作到 60 岁。 《环球时报》报道称：“从经济上来说，我不需要这份工作来谋生，但我喜欢这份工作的氛围，它让我保持健康。” “我想要脚踏实地的生活，这个奖项永远不会改变我是谁。” 《低空飞行》于 2024 年出版，是一本诗集，灵感来自于王对约 200 名送货骑手进行的采访和调查。 “谁说展翅高飞？低飞也是飞翔。”他的诗中有这样一句话。 他的获奖之际，近年来，越来越多的中国蓝领工人在文学界崭露头角。 前快递员胡安彦于 2023 年出版的回忆录《我在北京送包裹》在中国成为畅销书，也引起了海外媒体的关注。该回忆录的英文译本于去年出版......

reflection.en: This story reminds us that every form of honest labor holds dignity, and talent can emerge from any walk of life. Yahweh calls us to approach all our work, no matter how humble, with diligence and excellence, as if serving Him directly. Such dedication often reveals hidden gifts and brings unexpected honor.

body.en: Startling new research shows that in many countries – including old US allies – the public prefers Beijing to Washington Earlier this year, a spate of western TikTok and Instagram creators announced that they were at “a very Chinese time in my life” – drinking hot water and wearing slippers around their homes. The Chinamaxxing phenomenon primarily reflected the constant need of influencers for novel content. But social media trends also reflect a growing fascination with China, as the economic historian Adam Tooze has noted . While it broods over China’s economic, military and technical advance, the Trump administration is accelerating Beijing’s diplomatic progress, as striking new polling by the Pew Research Center shows. For the first time, China and Xi Jinping are seen more favourably than the US and its president in most of the 36 major countries surveyed – including Canada, Mexico and Australia. Only in six countries did people rate the US more highly. While Beijing has seen significant improvements in some places, the slump in Washington’s standing is more dramatic. Across 20 countries, the median percentage with a favourable view of China rose from 32% to 46% between 2023 and this year; for the US, it fell from 58% to 36%. Views of China were much more positive in Latin America, Africa and parts of south and south-east Asia than in wealthier European and east Asian countries. Continue reading...
body.zh: 令人震惊的新研究表明，在许多国家 — — 包括美国的老盟友 — — 公众更喜欢北京而不是华盛顿。 今年早些时候，一大批西方 TikTok 和 Instagram 创作者宣布，他们正处于“我一生中非常中国化的时期”——喝着热水，在家中穿着拖鞋。 Chinamaxshing现象主要反映了网红对新颖内容的持续需求。但正如经济历史学家亚当·图兹（Adam Tooze）指出的那样，社交媒体趋势也反映出人们对中国日益增长的迷恋。皮尤研究中心令人震惊的最新民意调查显示，在关注中国经济、军事和技术进步的同时，特朗普政府正在加速北京的外交进展。在接受调查的 36 个主要国家（包括加拿大、墨西哥和澳大利亚）中，大多数国家对中国和习近平的好感度首次高于美国及其总统。只有六个国家的人们对美国的评价更高。尽管北京在某些方面取得了显着进步，但华盛顿的地位下滑更为严重。 2023 年至今，20 个国家对中国持好感的中位数百分比从 32% 上升至 46%；美国则从 58% 下降至 36%。拉丁美洲、非洲以及南亚和东南亚部分地区对中国的看法比富裕的欧洲和东亚国家要积极得多。继续阅读...

Proverbs 14:34 suggests that righteousness elevates a people, while moral failings can bring disgrace. This perspective encourages us to consider how nations, like individuals, are ultimately judged...
reflection.zh: 新闻中强调的全球对超级大国看法的转变，提醒我们一个国家真正的地位往往与其品格和行为息息相关。箴言14:34指出，公义使邦国高举，罪恶是人民的羞辱。这一视角鼓励我们思考，国家如同个人，最终会因其正直和所体现的价值观而受到评判。

verse.textEn: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin condemns any people.
verse.textZh: 公义使邦国高举；罪恶是人民的羞辱。

title.en: Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own | Jamil Smith
title.zh: 特朗普援引外国选举干预来为自己辩护 | 贾米尔·史密斯

summary.en: An article discusses how the former president's claims of foreign election interference are used to justify his own actions, leading him to treat voters who opposed him as suspects rather than legitimate participants in the democratic process.
summary.zh: 一篇文章讨论了前总统如何援引外国选举干预来为自己的行为辩护，导致他将反对他的选民视为嫌疑犯，而非民主进程的合法参与者。

body.en: The president no longer treats the people who defeated him as voters. He treats them as suspects There is a version of this country in which Donald Trump tells Americans the truth he has been handed: that their elections are secure. Once, he apparently wanted to. The Atlantic reported after Thursday night’s address that a February 2020 election-security briefing pleased Trump so much he wanted to announce the news himself. The press conference never happened. The election did, and Trump lost it. Continue reading...
body.zh: 总统不再将击败他的人视为选民。他将他们视为嫌疑人。这个国家有一个版本，唐纳德·特朗普告诉美国人他所得到的真相：他们的选举是安全的。有一次，他显然想要这么做。 《大西洋月刊》在周四晚上的讲话后报道称，2020 年 2 月的选举安全简报令特朗普非常高兴，他想亲自宣布这一消息。新闻发布会从未发生过。选举确实发生了，但特朗普输了。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news highlights how a leader's refusal to accept election results and subsequent treatment of citizens as "suspects" can undermine trust and civic harmony. Proverbs 29:2 reminds us that the character of those in authority profoundly impacts the well-being of the people. When leaders govern with integrity and truth, society flourishes; when they do not,...

verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: China firm seeks damages over state control of British Steel
title.zh: 中国公司就英国钢铁国有化寻求赔偿

summary.en: China's Jingye Group is seeking compensation from the UK government after the government took over British Steel last year. The UK government intervened to prevent the closure of the country's last primary steelmaking facility, which Jingye Group had purchased in 2020.
summary.zh: 中国敬业集团正向英国政府寻求赔偿，此前英国政府去年接管了英国钢铁公司，以防止该国最后一个主要炼钢设施关闭。敬业集团于2020年收购了该公司。

body.en:
The UK government took over British Steel last year to prevent the closure of the country's last primary steelmaking facility. China's Jingye Group, which bought the firm in 2020, claims it is owed compensation.

A Chinese steel giant demanded compensation from the United Kingdom   government on Sunday, claiming the state's takeover of its subsidiary, British Steel, was "outright robbery."

The UK government took operational control of British Steel last year, after owner Jingye Group warned that Britain's last factory capable of making steel from scratch was no longer financially viable.

In a statement on social media, Jingye threatened legal action against the UK government, accusing ministers of "trampling on international investment rules."

Describing the nationalization as "outright robbery," the Chinese firm said it "reserves all legal rights, firmly defends its lawful rights and interests, and will pursue full compensation through legal means to the very end."

"The UK disregarded Jingye's continuous investment and significant contribution and was only willing to provide almost zero compensation,” the statement continued.

The company noted that nationalization could cost UK taxpayers more than 1.5 billion pounds ($2.02 billion, €1.76 billion) by 2028.

Jingye said it had begun a procedure under bilateral investment agreements to seek damages, without expanding further.

China's Foreign Ministry backed the compensation move, calling on the UK to "earnestly respect market principles and the spirit of contract, and find solutions on compensation and other issues acceptable to both sides."

After Jingye last year planned to close the blast furnaces at its plant in Scunthorpe, in northern England, the UK government passed emergency measures, allowing it to take  operational control of British Steel .

The immediate concern was that the blast furnaces would be shut permanently, ending the UK's capacity to produce virgin or primary steel from raw materials. The plant accounts for the vast majority of British Steel's operations.

The government cited national security for the move, which came five years after Jingye bought British Steel from a London-based private equity firm for around 70 million pounds.

Ministers cited the need to protect strategic steel supplies for construction, rail infrastructure and defense.

The move was also seen as a way to protect thousands of jobs in a deprived area of the UK. The Scunthorpe plant currently employs about 2,700 people.

In recent weeks, the UK Parliament has passed legislation that allowed the government on Thursday to bring British Steel into full public ownership.

body.zh: 英国政府去年接管了英国钢铁公司，以防止该国最后一个主要炼钢厂关闭。于 2020 年收购该公司的中国敬业集团声称其被欠赔偿。 周日，一家中国钢铁巨头要求英国政府赔偿，声称英国政府对其子公司英国钢铁公司的收购是“彻头彻尾的抢劫”。 去年，英国政府接管了英国钢铁公司的运营控制权，此前其所有者敬业集团警告称，英国最后一家能够从头开始生产钢铁的工厂不再具有财务可行性。 在周六社交媒体上的一份声明中，敬业威胁要对英国政府采取法律行动，指责部长们“践踏国际投资规则”。 这家中国公司将此次国有化描述为“彻头彻尾的抢劫”，并表示“保留一切合法权利，坚决捍卫合法权益，并将通过法律手段追究到底”。 声明还说：“英国无视敬业公司的持续投资和重大贡献，只愿意提供几乎为零的补偿。” 该公司指出，到 2028 年，国有化可能会让英国纳税人损失超过 15 亿英镑（20.2 亿美元，17.6 亿欧元）。 敬业表示，已根据双边投资协议启动了寻求损害赔偿的程序，但没有进一步扩大范围。 中国外交部支持这一赔偿举措，呼吁英方“切实尊重市场原则和契约精神，就赔偿等问题找到双方都能接受的解决方案”。 去年敬业计划关闭位于英格兰北部斯肯索普工厂的高炉后，英国政府通过了紧急措施，允许其对英国钢铁公司进行运营控制。 当务之急是高炉将永久关闭，从而结束英国利用原材料生产原生钢的能力。该工厂占英国钢铁公司业务的绝大多数。 政府以国家安全为由采取了这一举措，五年前敬业以约 7000 万英镑从一家伦敦私募股权公司手中收购了英国钢铁公司 (British Steel)。 部长们指出有必要保护建筑、铁路基础设施和国防的战略钢铁供应。 此举也被视为保护英国贫困地区数千个就业岗位的一种方式。 斯肯索普工厂目前拥有约 2,700 名员工。 最近几周，英国议会通过了一项立法，允许政府于周四将英国钢铁公司完全纳入公有制。 根据新法律，独立评估师必须评估是否有...

reflection.en: When governments intervene in economic affairs, the call for justice and righteousness remains paramount. Yahweh's word reminds leaders to act fairly, ensuring that all parties, including investors, are treated equitably and not unjustly deprived. This principle encourages thoughtful consideration of compensation and fair dealings in complex situations...
reflection.zh: 当政府干预经济事务时，对公义和正直的呼吁至关重要。雅伟的话语提醒领导者要公正行事，确保包括投资者在内的所有各方都受到公平对待，不被不公正地剥夺。这一原则鼓励在涉及国家利益和私营企业的复杂情况下，深思熟虑赔偿和公平交易。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Trump, not Iran, is the world’s greatest danger. He’s a one-man weapon of mass destruction | Simon Tisdall
title.zh: 特朗普，而非伊朗，是世界上最大的危险。他是一个人的大规模杀伤性武器 | 西蒙·蒂斯代尔

summary.en: The article argues that the US president's actions have initiated a disastrous war and an economic quagmire, leading to a "limitless fiasco" as bombing resumes. It characterizes the president as "feckless and clueless," unable to navigate or exit the conflict he started.
summary.zh: 文章指出，随着轰炸再次开始，美国总统的行为已将美国拖入一场无止境的灾难和经济泥潭。文章形容这位总统“无能又糊涂”，无法摆脱他所发动的这场灾难性战争。

body.en: As the bombing starts again, it’s clear the president has dragged the US into a limitless fiasco – and the world into an economic quagmire Feckless and clueless, Donald Trump is lost in Iran, unable to find a way out of the disastrous war he started. Once again, the US military is pummelling the country and, increasingly, its civilian infrastructure. As before, this unlawful bludgeoning strengthens the resistance of a hardline regime that cares little for its people’s suffering. How often have Trump and Pete Hegseth, the Pentagon’s wildling lord of bones, hailed a bogus victory? The president claimed this week to be “winning big”. No one believes him. Even as it counts the vast human and economic cost of his Persian folly, a watching world scoffs at US impotence. Control of the strait of Hormuz, closed due to Trump’s belligerence, is now the White House’s limited, elusive objective. The grander US and Israeli war aims – eliminating Iran’s nuclear programme, degrading its regional militias, regime change – are less attainable than ever. It’s Trump’s craven leadership that renders US forces ineffective, not the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. If Iran really is the existential menace he claims, the logical course would be all-out conquest. When George W Bush decided Iraq posed unacceptable dangers, he invaded with 170,000 ground troops. It was a catastrophe. But at least Bush had balls. Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator Continue reading...
body.zh: 随着轰炸再次开始，很明显，总统已将美国拖入了无限的惨败 — — 并将世界拖入了经济泥潭。 无能又无能的唐纳德·特朗普在伊朗迷失了方向，无法找到摆脱他发起的灾难性战争的出路。美国军队再次对该国进行打击，并越来越多地打击其民用基础设施。和以前一样，这种非法的殴打加强了一个不关心人民苦难的强硬政权的抵抗。特朗普和五角大楼的野人骸骨领主皮特·赫格斯多少次欢呼一场虚假的胜利？总统本周声称“大获全胜”。没有人相信他。尽管他的波斯愚蠢行为造成了巨大的人力和经济成本，但全世界都在嘲笑美国的无能。控制因特朗普的好战而关闭的霍尔木兹海峡，现在已成为白宫有限且难以捉摸的目标。美国和以色列更宏伟的战争目标——消除伊朗核计划、削弱其地区民兵、政权更迭——比以往任何时候都更难以实现。导致美军效率低下的是特朗普胆怯的领导，而不是伊斯兰革命卫队。如果伊朗确实是他所声称的生存威胁，那么合乎逻辑的路线将是全面征服。当乔治·W·布什认定伊拉克构成了无法接受的危险时，他派遣了 17 万地面部队入侵。这是一场灾难。但至少布什有胆量。西蒙·蒂斯达尔是卫报外交事务评论员继续阅读...

reflection.en: This proverb reminds us of the profound and often devastating impact that leaders can have on their people and the world. When those in power act recklessly or without wisdom, the consequences can be like a destructive force, leaving nations in turmoil and people vulnerable. It underscores the heavy responsibility of leadership and the need for discernment...
reflection.zh: 这句箴言提醒我们，领袖对他们的人民和世界可能产生深刻而往往是毁灭性的影响。当掌权者鲁莽行事或缺乏智慧时，其后果可能像一股破坏性的力量，使国家陷入混乱，人民变得脆弱。它强调了领导的重任以及对执政者保持明辨的重要性。

verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.zh: 事实核查唐纳德·特朗普关于中国干预选举的讲话——视频

The Guardian's voting rights reporter Sam Levine factchecks some of Trump's claims Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own - Opinion Continue reading...

This story reminds us of the importance of careful scrutiny and hearing all sides, especially when serious allegations are made. Yahweh encourages us to seek wisdom and not to accept every statement at face value.
reflection.zh: 在公共讨论中，最初的说法往往听起来很有说服力，直到它们被彻底审查。这个故事提醒我们，仔细审查和听取各方意见的重要性，尤其是在提出严重指控时。雅伟鼓励我们寻求智慧，不要轻信每一个说法。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: Beijing’s message to the world’s tourists: come here and judge China for yourselves | Zichen Wang
title.zh: 北京向世界游客发出信息：来中国，亲自评判

summary.en: Beijing has relaxed its visa rules, aiming to boost its economy and enhance its international image. The move has led to a noticeable return of foreign tourists to the capital, engaging in sightseeing and local activities.
summary.zh: 北京放宽了签证规定，旨在提振经济并改善其国际形象。此举已使外国游客明显回流首都，他们正在观光并参与当地活动。

body.en: By relaxing visa rules, Beijing has two things on its mind – boosting its economy and improving its self-image Walk through central Beijing today and one thing quickly becomes apparent: foreigners are back. They are taking photos outside the Forbidden City and sitting in cafes around Gulou and Sanlitun. The shift is visible online, too; YouTube is increasingly filled with videos titled “China Shocked Me” or “My First Week in China”. Most of the creators are tourists, not China specialists or journalists, and many of them are encountering the country for the first time. The resurgence is striking because to many outside observers China’s story has become one of closure and increased security – of intensifying strategic rivalry with the west, expanded anti-espionage enforcement and increasingly constrained foreign reporting, including the withholding and revocation of visas for US journalists. Yet on the ground, another story is unfolding. When it comes to its relationship with the rest of the world, Beijing increasingly appears to be betting on direct exposure: come to China and judge for yourself. Zichen Wang is deputy secretary-general at the Center for China and Globalization, a thinktank in Beijing. This article was co-written by Hao Wu, an assistant professor at the School of International Studies at Peking University Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? reflection.en: By inviting tourists to "judge China for yourselves," Beijing seeks to bridge gaps in understanding and perception. This echoes a deeper human longing to dismantle barriers and foster connection, reminding us that Yahweh desires for dividing walls of hostility to be broken down. Such direct encounters, even for economic reasons, can open pathways for...
reflection.zh: 北京邀请游客“亲自评判中国”，旨在弥合理解和认知上的鸿沟。这呼应了人类拆除隔阂、促进联结的深层渴望，提醒我们雅伟渴望拆毁敌意的隔墙。即使是出于经济原因，这种直接的接触也能为各民族之间更深的相互理解开辟道路。

verse.textEn: For he himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility.
verse.textZh: 因他使我们和睦，将两下合而为一，拆毁了中间隔断的墙。

title.en: 'Shocking vulnerabilities': Trump makes sweeping claims China meddled in US elections

summary.en: The US president made broad election security claims, laying groundwork for the federal government to take action.

body.en:
In a speech attacking US election integrity on Friday, US President Donald Trump released intelligence that he said showed major Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his false claims he won the 2020 election.

Trump's allegations about the "shocking vulnerabilities" in the American electoral system appeared to lay the groundwork for the Republican to dispute the results of November's crucial US midterm elections .

It underscored Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm vote, when Republicans in Congress will face the prospect of losing control of both the House of Representatives and Senate — an outcome that would carry significant political consequences for Trump.

"We can never watch a stolen election again," Trump said in the primetime address, referencing his 2020 presidential election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden.

Trump said he was declassifying huge amounts of intelligence data that showed, among other things, that superpower rival China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files.

"Over a period of years, starting during the 2020 election cycle, the People's Republic of China carried out what is believed to be the largest compromise of election data in history," Trump said in the televised speech from the White House.

He asserted that members of the US intelligence community deliberately suppressed information about the extent of China's activities.

His allegations contradict an unclassified 2021 US intelligence community assessment that found no indications any foreign actor tried to alter or succeeded in altering "any technical aspect" of the 2020 presidential election vote.

The assessment was conducted under John Ratcliffe, then Trump's director of national intelligence and now his CIA director.

Trump also claimed there were more than 250,000 non-US citizens registered to vote in four states.

Trump has persistently claimed his 2020 election defeat was "rigged," although more than 60 lawsuits produced no ruling establishing fraud capable of changing the outcome, while recounts, audits and his own justice department found none.

After railing against election security in the 25-minute address, Trump pressed Republicans in Congress to pass his signature elections legislation, the SAVE America Act, which has been stalled for months.

It seeks to impose new voter identification and citizenship requirements, despite longstanding findings that voter fraud in US elections is rare.

Election security experts have said these measures would make it harder for millions of eligible voters to cast a ballot.

title.en: Israel's embassy takes rare swipe at Labor's platform on eve of conference

summary.en: The four-page statement drew a shrug from a member of Labor's front bench.

body.en:
Israel's embassy has rebuked the Labor party's draft national platform, warning its wording on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict places sole "responsibility" on the Jewish state while overlooking the role of Hamas and Palestinian leadership.

The four-page statement is a highly unusual intervention by a foreign government ahead of the party's national conference in Adelaide.

Labor's 2026 platform, which outlines the party's priorities and beliefs, contains an expanded statement on "Israel and Palestine" following the government's move to recognise Palestinian statehood, a longstanding part of the party platform.

The document reiterates support for a two-state solution, and also says the party "unreservedly condemns terrorism and violent extremism, including as perpetrated by Hamas and other extremists," stating Israelis and Palestinians deserve to live their lives free from terror and violence.

The platform says Israel "must comply with obligations as an occupying power" in supplying food and medical supplies for Palestinian civilians under international humanitarian law, and also condemns recent Knesset laws around the death penalty as "discriminatory."

The 'Death Penalty for Terrorists' law passed in March — and a subsequent 2026 military tribunal law — mandate capital punishment for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks. The United Nations Human Rights Office warned the laws breach international humanitarian law and could amount to war crimes.

The unsigned Israeli embassy statement, released on Monday, reads: "The Embassy respectfully submits that several elements of the draft National Platform risk placing responsibility for the conflict on one party while giving insufficient attention to the decisions, conduct and continuing obligations of the Palestinian leadership and terrorist organisations such as Hamas."

"Israel has repeatedly demonstrated its willingness to make difficult compromises when genuine peace is possible."

While continuing to oppose Palestinian recognition, which the Australian government declared sovereign and independent in September 2025, Israel's embassy also disputed language in the draft platform condemning "extremist settler violence," which the government in June warned was at "horrific levels".

The embassy said settler violence "receives disproportionate attention," labelling it a "reprehensible but marginal phenomenon".

UN monitors have documented over 1,000 Israeli settler attacks causing casualties or property damage this year, averaging six incidents per day and resulting in the displacement of more than 2,200 Palestinians.

title.en: The Tate brothers' international legal saga: The cases, charges and what comes next
title.zh: 泰特兄弟的国际法律纠葛：案件、指控及后续发展

summary.en: Self-described misogynist Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were arrested over the weekend in the US and face charges in multiple jurisdictions.

body.en:
On Sunday, social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested in Miami in the United States, after authorities in the United Kingdom issued 38 new charges against the brothers, deepening the pair's international legal saga and adding further complication to an already fraught legal situation.

The United Kingdom's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has charged the brothers — who deny all wrongdoing — with fresh counts of rape, actual bodily harm, and human trafficking.

The new accusations add to a mountain of serious charges against the pair and could lead to the brothers' extradition from the US, assuming it is approved by the US state department.

Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate are dual US-UK citizens who have risen to prominence as social media influencers.

Andrew started his career in public life as a kickboxer and has gone on to become a prominent figure in the online 'manosphere' space, describing himself as a misogynist and encouraging his more than 10 million followers to follow in his footsteps.

He primarily posts on X, having been banned from YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram for violating hate speech guidelines.

Stephanie Wescott, a lecturer in humanities and social science at Monash University, described Andrew as the "main character" of this content, while his brother Tristan is more of a "side figure".

She said the Tates have turned disrespecting and abusing women into a business model that glamorises male dominance, 'teaching' men how to emulate them through an online academy.

"[They promote] anti-feminism, anti-gender-equality, and hyper-masculinity or, you know, 'men being men' or men going back to a type of manhood that no longer exists," she said.

"One of their business models has been to train other young men into becoming the sort of influencers that they claim that they are.

"Part of that business model has also been to exploit and harm the girls and women around you and to use their images as currency to sell online — we know Australian men have signed up for these services.

The pair have also expressed support for US President Donald Trump, and Trump's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr, spoke out against the brothers' detention in Romania in 2023.

"The other layer to this is, of course, that they have this incredible political proximity to Donald Trump," Wescott said.

In 2025, Andrew Tate said he was "very close with the Trump family". Trump himself has said little about the Tates, however.

"They have been supported and aided by adjacent figures, podcasters such as Joe Rogan and others like him," Wescott continued.

title.en: Nigel Farage's unusual UK by-election now has an Australian candidate

summary.en: Nigel Farage will compete in the Clacton by-election against several candidates, including Count Binface and Australian Daniel Pocock.
summary.zh: 奈杰尔·法拉奇将在克拉克顿补选中与包括宾费斯伯爵和澳大利亚人丹尼尔·波科克在内的多位候选人竞争。

body.en:
There's a man with a bin on his head, three people representing the Monster Raving Loony Party, Nigel Farage and an Australian — now all vying for the seat vacated by the Reform UK leader in a crucial by-election.

The Clacton by-election, triggered by the parliamentary resignation of Farage over a donations scandal, has attracted all sorts of profiles to the mix.

Farage, who is under investigation over millions of pounds' worth of undeclared gifts and donations from wealthy backers, quit parliament earlier this month to trigger a by-election, but said he would re-contest his seat . The Reform UK leader said he wanted voters in his electoral district in south-east England to judge his actions, not what he said was a liberal "establishment" bent on discrediting him.

Farage is widely expected to win the seat again, and is the only mainstream candidate running, after other major parties said they would refuse to take part in what they characterised as a stunt.

A number of joke candidates — including Count Binface and another called 'Nick the Incredible Flying Brick' — are vying for the seat, along with 20 independents.

Pocock is a Swiss-Irish-Australian software engineer who describes himself as an "expert on cybersecurity, open source software [and] cryptocurrencies".

According to his website, he was born in the Melbourne suburb of Coburg before moving to rural Wandong. He graduated from the University of Melbourne in 2002 with a Bachelor of Computer Science.

While studying, he joined the National Union of Students and used his technical skills to assist websites for early social causes. He built a website opposing the death penalty after Schapelle Corby's arrest in Bali on drug trafficking charges.

He moved to Europe after graduation and worked for companies like Barclays Capital, Thomson Reuters, and UBS.

In a press release announcing his candidacy, Pocock says he was spurred to nominate himself for Clacton by the prospect of "novelty candidates".

"If the Essex Lion was to appear on the ballot paper, I suspect it would have an equally good chance of winning. I have yet to see a single report about the real, day-to-day issues facing residents of the district," he said.

"In a parody of this situation, I have chosen the codename Pocock-on-Sea for the operation to unleash an Australian upon London's Establishment."

title.en: Legendary media figure Derryn Hinch makes his final headlines with state funeral
title.zh: 传奇媒体人物德林·辛奇 (Derryn Hinch) 因国葬而成为最后的头条新闻

summary.en: Outspoken media figure and former senator Derryn Hinch died earlier this month at the age of 82, after a long and public health battle.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Derryn Hinch has been remembered for making waves as one of Australia's most outspoken and influential voices.

Longtime friend and colleague Darren James led mourners through a state funeral for the former broadcaster and senator on Monday.

"He was a journalist, a newspaper reporter, a TV presenter, a godfather, an author, a senator and, a prisoner ... he did it all," James told the service.

Hinch died on 10 July at the age of 82 after a lengthy health struggle , much of which he documented for followers on social media.

The service for the lifelong atheist, who went to jail for identifying a paedophile Catholic priest before his trial, was held at the Timber Yard events space in Port Melbourne, near factories and apartments devoid of any religious leaning.

It attracted notable figures, including news presenters Ray Martin and Denis Walter, entertainers Rhonda Burchmore and Greg Evans, and former Crown executive Ann Peacock.

Other mourners, including Labor MP Danny Pearson, who attended on behalf of Premier Jacinta Allan, streamed in to pay their respects.

"Not all of us knew him personally, but for many it felt like we did," Pearson said.

An Australian flag was draped over his casket, surrounded by vases of red roses symbolising deep love, respect, courage and enduring affection.

Hinch initially moved from New Zealand to Australia to pursue a career in journalism, climbing the ranks to become editor of The Sun before turning to a career in radio.

He became known as the "human headline" — a moniker he enthusiastically adopted — for his outspoken and often controversial opinions.

Former 3AW colleagues Denis O'Kane and Tony Tardio spoke of their love for Hinch, who was well known for his hatred of child sex offenders and those who shielded them.

"He was a journalistic James Bond, drama followed him everywhere — even to his first wedding. And then he went on to marry three other times."

His ex-wife and friend, actor Jacki Weaver, sent a video tribute from America describing Hinch as a wonderful stepfather and companion.

"I'd like to pay my respects to all the women who loved Derryn, and who loved him back," she said.

While commanding the airwaves for decades as a talkback radio host on Melbourne radio station 3AW, Hinch became known for his uninhibited takes and a tendency to court controversy.

Later, Hinch turned to the political arena, forming Derryn Hinch's Justice Party and serving as a senator for Victoria in the federal parliament from 2016 to 2019.
